ledger: Wind: no evidence of wind. Trees, cloud shapes and the loose black T-shirt and pants show no fluttering anywhere in 00:00-00:09.75. All consistently still, so no inconsistency.

Rolling motion (00:00-01.25, 03.75-07.75, 09.25-09.75): skater rolls on flat concrete. Clothing shows only mild motion from the body's own movement. Background motion comes from the moving low-angle fisheye camera, not from deformation. Consistent.

Sunlight/shadows: strong sun, upper frame. Skater and board shadows fall toward the camera or to the side across the rolling segments. While backlit (01.5-03.5) the shadow falls off-frame toward the camera, and it reappears on landing. Plausible.

Gravity, trick 1 (pop around 01.4, landing around 03.2): should produce a short parabolic arc of about 0.5 s on flat ground. Instead the skater and board hang at a nearly constant height from about 01.75 to 02.75 and only come down at about 03.0-03.25. Total airtime is about 1.6 s.

Gravity, trick 2 (pop around 07.9, landing around 09.25 near the bowl coping): airborne for about 1.2-1.3 s with a slow hover at peak height (08.25-08.75). The landing may be slightly lower, at the bowl edge, which partly explains the extra airtime.
Board during flips: rotates under the feet while airborne and comes back to the feet without any visible external force. The flip itself is normal skate physics. Only its timing is suspect.

findings.description: After popping off flat ground at about 01.4 s, the skater and board stay airborne until about 03.2 s, roughly 1.6 s. From about 01.75 to 02.75 they hover at nearly the same height in every frame, with no descent, before dropping. A flatground flip trick at this pop height should land in about 0.5 s. The rolling footage around it plays at normal speed, so slow motion doesn't explain the hang time.

On the second trick the skater pops at about 07.9 s and lands at about 09.25 s, roughly 1.3 s in the air. The body and the level board float at a near-constant peak height from about 08.25 to 08.75. That is longer than a normal ollie or flip allows, though a slightly lower landing at the bowl edge partly accounts for it.
